title: Policy Stance on "99-to-1" Arrangements for Stamp Duty Payment in Property Transactions and Measures to Prevent Recurrence
what_it_is: Policy Stance on "99-to-1" Arrangements for Stamp Duty Payment in Property Transactions and Measures to Prevent Recurrence

sections.label: 99-to-1 ABSD avoidance questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about 99-to-1 property purchases, IRAS audit letters in 2023, market impact, accountability steps, case numbers, owner relationships and investigation delay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what is the assessed number of cases in each year over the last five years where first-time buyers of private residential properties have signed fresh agreements to sell 1% of the same property shortly after exercising the purchase options; (b) how many audit letters have been sent by IRAS questioning such transactions in 2023; and (c) what is the impact of such transactions on the residential and mortgage markets in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in light of the probe by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) on property purchases structured in a "99-to-1" manner for the purpose of avoiding the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD), what are steps that the Government is considering to hold agents and other marketers of such potential tax avoidance schemes accountable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance regarding IRAS' investigation into cases of property purchases structured in a "99-to-1" manner to avoid the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) (a) how many cases have been uncovered so far; (b) what are the three most common relationships between the property owners; and (c) why has it taken IRAS more than a decade to start investigations as the ABSD was introduced in 2011.

sections.label: ABSD joint purchase and 99-to-1
sections.summary: ABSD on joint purchases uses the highest buyer profile, and section 33A lets the Commissioner disregard split steps; 0.5% of transactions from 2018 to 2021 involved such arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: When a residential property is jointly purchased by two or more buyers, the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) rate arising from the buyer with the highest ABSD profile will apply on the entire value of the purchase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Hence, when a single purchase is split up into two or more steps to reduce the tax payable, the Commissioner of Stamp Duties is empowered, under section 33A of the Stamp Duties Act, to disregard the individual steps and assess stamp duty as a single joint purchase and to recover the rightful amount of ABSD due.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2021, about 0.5% of private residential properties transacted involved such "99-to-1" or similar arrangements, where the owners sold a partial interest in their property to another buyer within a short period of time.

sections.label: IRAS recovery and 50% surcharge
sections.summary: If IRAS finds tax avoidance, it will recover the rightful stamp duty from buyers and may impose a 50% surcharge on the additional stamp duty payable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Should IRAS determine that tax avoidance has occurred, it will recover the rightful amount of stamp duty from the buyers and may impose a 50% surcharge on the additional stamp duty payable.

sections.label: Tax amount and ongoing investigations
sections.summary: The tax amount cannot yet be given as investigations are ongoing, but IRAS may require buyers to pay the full ABSD and a 50% surcharge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As to the amount of the tax that is payable, it is too early for me to give a number now because the investigations are still ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But if there are cases where the rightful amount of ABSD is not paid fully, as I mentioned in my reply, IRAS will be able to ask the buyers to pay for the full amount and may impose a 50% surcharge in such cases.
